title: Compact Suffix Rules for Stemming in Morphologically Rich Languages

headings.text: Compact Suffix Rules for Stemming in Morphologically Rich Languages

key_sentences: Stemming reduces inflected words to a common form and remains a cheap and effective step in retrieval pipelines.
On five morphologically rich languages the rules recover 93.8% of the accuracy of a full morphological analyser while using less than one percent of its memory.
Full morphological analysers solve this problem but need large lexicons and careful maintenance.
Rules are tried from the longest suffix to the shortest, and the first rule whose condition holds is applied.
Pairs that appear in both sets are removed from the test set.
The largest gains appear for Finnish and Hungarian, where long suffix chains are common.
Finnish needs the most rules because of its many cases and possessive suffixes.
Homographs are rare in Finnish but frequent in Czech, where many endings are shared by different cases.
We thank the annotators who checked the test pairs.

list_items.text: • a compact rule format that fits in a few kilobytes;
• a learning procedure that needs only lemma and form pairs;
• an evaluation on five languages with released test sets.
1. irregular stems, such as vowel changes inside the word;
2. homographs whose lemma depends on context;
[1] M. Hartmann. Light stemming for agglutinative languages. Journal of Text Processing, 12(3):45–61, 2019.
[2] S. Varga and P. Novak. Learning suffix rules from lemma lists. In Proceedings of the Workshop on Morphology, pages 101–110, 2021.
[3] R. Ito. A comparison of stemmers for search. Information Systems Review, 8(1):1–19, 2022.
